statement: The dollar will buy fewer Japanese yen on December 31, 2026 than on November 20, 2026.
why: The yen is near 160 per dollar even after close to 100 billion dollars of intervention. A Reuters poll found 86 of economists expect the Bank of Japan to raise rates to 1.50 at its December 17-18 meeting, and Governor Ueda says the bank should keep raising. A rate hike, a government ready to step in again and a nervous stock market all tend to strengthen the yen. I am wrong if the dollar buys more yen at year end than on November 20, for example because the Bank of Japan holds rates or the Fed's hike widens the gap between US and Japanese rates.

statement: The stock market's fear gauge will be lower on January 15, 2027 than at Friday's close near 36.
why: The VIX closed near 36 on November 20 after the S&P 500 fell into a correction and Nvidia lost about 14 in a single day. Readings this high rarely last for weeks, because fear tends to fade once the selling slows, even when prices do not fully recover. I expect it well below 30 by mid-January. I am wrong if the VIX closes on January 15 above Friday's close, for example because the SEC look at Nvidia's accounting grows into a wider crisis or a Fed hike sets off another leg down.
